messages.content: Write a polished 400-to-500-word contemporary American English scene between two consenting adults who have recently started dating. They are doing an ordinary errand together. Let the romantic interest show through ordinary attention, teasing, pauses, and small physical closeness rather than repeated declarations. Include one moment where they realize the relationship is becoming more serious, but keep it understated and realistic. Do not use explicit sexual detail or idealized romance language.

Casey pushed the cart toward the end of the hardware aisle.

“You're buying another screwdriver.”

Morgan looked at the shelf.

“This one is different.”

“They all look the same.”

“They absolutely do not.”

Casey smiled. “You said that last time.”

“I was right last time.”

“You're always right.”

Morgan looked over. “That sounded sarcastic.”

“It was.”

They turned the corner and stopped near a display of light bulbs.

Morgan picked up a package.

“What kind do you use?”

“The regular kind.”

“That tells me nothing.”

Casey laughed.

“Warm white.”

Morgan checked the label.

“These?”

“Yeah.”

She put the package in the cart.

“You didn't have to buy those.”

“I know.”

Casey looked at her.

Morgan shrugged.

“You said you needed them.”

“I could've gotten them.”

“I know that too.”

They kept walking.

At the register, Casey reached for her wallet.

“I've got it.”

Morgan shook her head.

“It's fine.”

“I said I've got it.”

Casey put her wallet away.

“You're stubborn.”

“You knew that.”

“I did.”

They left the store with two bags between them.

Outside, the wind caught one of the receipts and sent it skittering across the parking lot.

Morgan watched it go.

“Should we chase that?”

“No.”

“Good.”

They reached the car.

Casey opened the passenger door, then stopped.

“What?” Morgan asked.

“Nothing.”

Morgan waited.

Casey looked at the shopping bags.

“You put the things I needed in your list.”

Morgan glanced down.

“Did I?”

“Yeah.”

“You told me once.”

“A week ago.”

“I remembered.”

Casey smiled.

“That seems dangerous.”

Morgan laughed.

“Probably.”

Casey got into the car.

Morgan closed the trunk and came around to the driver's side.

“You know,” Casey said as she buckled her seat belt, “this is starting to feel suspiciously like dating.”

Morgan started the engine.

“Starting?”

Casey laughed.

“Okay.”

Morgan reached across the console and squeezed her hand once.

Casey turned her palm over and held on for another second.

Neither said anything about it when Morgan pulled out of the parking lot.
